checkpoints.name: chasing_positive_bodies_competitive
checkpoints.description: Theorem 3.6 of Bhattacharya-Buchbinder-Levin-Saranurak (arXiv 2304.01889v2, = Theorem 1.1): for every chasing instance (epsilon in (0,1], positive weights, covering/packing halfspace sequence with covering row sparsity at most d >= 1) and every response satisfying the KKT bundle of Section 3.1, the upward recourse is at most K = (2+epsilon)(1+epsilon)log(1+40d^2/epsilon^2)/epsilon times the upward recourse of every exactly-feasible benchmark trajectory starting at 0.
